back: Pulling an answer out of memory instead of reading it again
explanation: Testing yourself is a way to learn and not only a way to check.

back: Being tested on something makes you remember it longer than studying it again

front: Why does rereading feel like it works?
back: The text becomes familiar and familiar feels like knowing
explanation: Recognising a page is easier than recalling what it says.

back: Spreading reviews of the same thing over days and weeks
Studying the same thing many times in one sitting

front: When is the best time to review something?
back: Shortly before you would forget it
explanation: A little forgetting makes the review harder and more useful.

front: You have 2 hours for one topic before an exam next month. Which plan helps you remember most on exam day?
choices: One 2-hour session tonight|Four 30-minute sessions spread over the month|Two hours of rereading the night before|One 2-hour session the morning of the exam
explanation: Spread over time the same 2 hours are remembered for longer. The night before feels best but fades fastest.

back: Mixing different topics or problem types in one session, not finishing one before the next

front: Why does mixed practice help with look-alikes?
back: You have to notice what tells them apart each time
explanation: In a block of one type you already know which type comes next.

front: During practice, mixing feels harder and your score is lower than in blocks. What does that tell you?
choices: Mixing is not working for you|Nothing yet: how practice feels is a poor guide to what you will remember later|You should go back to blocks|You are tired
explanation: Blocks look better while you practise and mixing looks better on a later test.

back: Effort while learning that slows you down now but helps you remember later
explanation: Recalling, spacing and mixing are examples.

front: What is the illusion of knowing?
back: Feeling sure you know something because it is familiar or was just in front of you

front: How can you check whether you really know something?
back: Close the book and try to say or write it from memory

front: You miss a card and then see the answer. Was that a waste?
back: No. A wrong try followed by the answer helps you remember it
explanation: Mistakes you were sure of are corrected especially well.

front: What does sleep do for what you learned today?
back: It helps to keep it: memories are strengthened during sleep
explanation: A short review the next morning uses this.

front: Which works better: one long session a week or a few minutes most days?
explanation: Short sessions give you spacing for free.
